# cockpit

> This index routes an unfamiliar agent to cockpit's setup and reference owners. cockpit runs the environment AI coding agents work in: one `cockpit.toml` declares the repositories, services and ports; `cockpit sync` renders agent surfaces and a Docker Compose stack over live checkouts; `cockpit check` fails on drift; and an independent evaluator (experimental) grades finished work. It is pre-alpha and not yet published.

## Set cockpit up

- [Agent adoption guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/agent-adoption.md): the safety contract and exact non-interactive commands for an agent adopting cockpit, by situation
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/README.md): what cockpit is, the quickstart, and its current limits
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/getting-started.md): install, bootstrap and the canonical bring-up sequence

## Reference

- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/cli-reference.md): every command, flag, exit code and diagnostic
- [Configuration reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/configuration-reference.md): every `cockpit.toml` field, the defaults and the JSON Schema
- [Concepts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/docs/concepts.md): the terms the commands and diagnostics use

## Contributing

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/b0dea/cockpit/main/AGENTS.md): the working guide for agents changing cockpit itself
